questions.question: Should there be a /achievements command and a menu button, since it is only in /tags now?
questions.suggested: Yes, add /achievements and a /menu button.
questions.why: Hard to find a feature hidden in the tags menu.

questions.question: Should the unlock chat line be hidden for tier-1 achievements to reduce spam?
questions.suggested: Show tier 1 only as the sound plus action bar; chat and title for higher tiers.
questions.why: New players unlock many things in the first hour.

questions.question: Should staff have a tool to give or reset an achievement for a player (bugs, support)?
questions.suggested: Yes: admin tool in /inspect.
questions.why: Needed if a tracker bug misses progress.

questions.question: Should there be achievement points (a total score) shown on the profile and in a leaderboard?
questions.suggested: Yes later: points per tier, a top list for the season.
questions.why: Gives completionists a goal.

questions.question: Which achievements should be added before launch (farming, fishing, bosses, KOTH, crates, voting, island level)?
questions.suggested: Add them with each feature; 60-80 total at launch.
questions.why: Each new system needs its own achievements.

features.summary: Donor ranks will get small convenience commands: crafting table anywhere, ender chest anywhere, wear an item as a hat, a custom nickname (with ~ marker), and a trash menu. Staff also have /repair and /realname, and the owner has /sudo. Right now only staff and ops have them until the donor ranks exist.

commands.what: Open a crafting table anywhere.
Open your ender chest anywhere.
Wear the held item as a hat.
Set or remove a nickname (3-16 characters, letters/numbers/_, shown with ~).
Menu where items you leave are destroyed on close.
Set or remove another player's nickname.
Find the real account behind a nickname.
Repair vanilla item durability.
Owner only: run a command or chat as a player (audited).

test: Give yourself the perk with LuckPerms (for example lp user <you> permission set skyblock.perks.craft true) and test /craft, /ec, /hat, /trash.
/nick Phoenix2: you get a ~ in front, the tab and chat show it, and /realname Phoenix2 shows your real name to staff.
Try a reserved nickname (admin, owner, staff), another player's name, and a nickname within 60 seconds of the last change. All refused.
Remove the nick permission: the nickname is reset when the rank that allowed it is lost.
Put a custom item (a tool or enchant book) in /trash and close it: check the warning in chat and that the item is gone and logged.
As mod: /repair hand on a damaged vanilla pickaxe. Custom tools have no durability.
As owner: /sudo <player> c:hello. Check the audit log.
Bedrock: open /trash and /ec and check taps work.

questions.question: Which rank gets which perk (suggested ladder in the next column)?
questions.suggested: Ladder: Ember (free) nothing; Squire /hat, colored chat, /trash; Knight /craft, profile slot 2; Paladin /ec, /nick; Warlord profile slot 3, hex chat; Monarch all plus more loadouts.
questions.why: This is the single biggest perk decision and is still open in the rank table.

questions.question: Should /trash refuse valuable custom items (tools, enchant books, set tokens, keys) unless you click a second confirm?
questions.suggested: Yes, a second confirm for custom items.
questions.why: Today the items are destroyed. A mis-click is expensive.

questions.question: Where should /ec and /craft be blocked: warzone, boss arena, during combat, events?
questions.suggested: Blocked in the warzone, boss arena and for 10 seconds after combat.
questions.why: Quick inventory access in fights is an unfair advantage.

questions.question: Should the nickname cooldown (60 seconds now) be longer, for example 1 hour?
questions.suggested: 1 hour.
questions.why: Frequent changes confuse other players and make staff work harder.

questions.question: Should nicknames be allowed for the free Ember rank?
questions.suggested: No. Nicknames start with the first paid rank.
questions.why: Keeps the free rank purely cosmetic.

questions.question: Should nicknames with colors and gradients be a separate higher perk than plain nicknames?
questions.suggested: Plain nick: Paladin; colors: Warlord; gradients/hex: Monarch.
questions.why: Natural step ladder.

questions.question: Should /ec open the ender chest of the profile you are on (yes, as built) or have a shared account chest?
questions.suggested: Per profile (decided for money and items).
questions.why: Confirms no item can move between profiles.

questions.question: Should donors have /repair on a long cooldown (for example once per hour) for vanilla tools?
questions.suggested: No. Mending exists and custom tools have no durability.
questions.why: Avoid giving away what XP and anvils already do.

questions.question: Should nicknames be shown in public join/quit lines and kill messages or only in chat?
questions.suggested: Everywhere the real name is hidden except staff tools.
questions.why: A nickname that sometimes shows the real name is confusing.

questions.question: Should /hat be allowed to wear any item (blocks, custom items) or a safe list only?
questions.suggested: Any normal item. Custom/unique items refused.
questions.why: Hats on custom tools could hide them from checks.

questions.question: Should staff be able to see all players' nicknames in the tab list in staff mode?
questions.suggested: Yes: staff see name and nickname.
questions.why: Moderation needs real names fast.

features.feature: Ranks, the free Ember rank and staff ranks
features.summary: Staff ranks exist now: Builder, Helper, Moderator, Admin, Owner, with colors and prefixes. A free rank called Ember can be claimed with /freerank after 30 minutes of total playtime and gives a colored name and a choice of one of three tags. Five paid donor ranks (Squire, Knight, Paladin, Warlord, Monarch) are planned with the store.

commands.what: After 30 minutes of playtime claim the free Ember rank once and pick 1 of 3 tags.
Staff ranks are handed out by the owner in LuckPerms; there is no in-game rank command.

test: Use a new account. Type /freerank before 30 minutes: you get a message with the time left.
After 30 minutes (or ask staff to raise your playtime) type /freerank. You get the Ember rank and a menu with three tags (ember, spark, ash). Pick one.
Type /freerank again: 'already claimed'. Relog: rank and tag stay.
Check chat and tab show the [Ember] prefix in its color. Check you do not get a join message (only ranks with that permission do).
Ask the owner to give a test account the helper rank: check prefix, color, staff chat and tab sorting.
Check /profiles shows slot 2 locked until you have 500 gems or Knight (when donor ranks exist).

questions.question: Are the five donor rank names final: Squire, Knight, Paladin, Warlord, Monarch?
questions.suggested: Yes, as proposed.
questions.why: Names are used in menus, profiles, loadouts and the store.

questions.question: Are donor ranks permanent (bought once with credits) or temporary (for example 30 days)?
questions.suggested: Permanent, kept across seasons.
questions.why: The biggest decision for how the store feels and what players will pay.

questions.question: If a player upgrades from Knight to Warlord, do they pay only the difference?
questions.suggested: Yes, pay the difference.
questions.why: Standard, fair and simple for players.

questions.question: Which gameplay advantages may ranks give, if any (profile slots, sell bonus up to +15%, progress boost 2-10%, AH slots)?
questions.suggested: Convenience and cosmetics only. Drop the progress boost; keep profile slots (also buyable with gems) and AH slots.
questions.why: Pay-to-win can hurt players' trust, and Mojang's commercial rules limit selling gameplay advantages.

questions.question: Should donor prefixes look different from staff prefixes (not bold, softer colors) so nobody mistakes a donor for staff?
questions.suggested: Yes: staff bold capitals in strong colors, donors normal capitals in soft colors.
questions.why: Prevents impersonation and scams.

questions.question: Which ranks get a join/quit message in chat (today only staff)?
questions.suggested: Knight and above; everyone can hide them in /settings.
questions.why: A fun perk, but spammy if every rank has it.

questions.question: Should /freerank count only active (non-AFK) playtime?
questions.suggested: Yes. AFK time does not count.
questions.why: Stops people from getting it by standing still.

questions.question: Should a trainee/junior helper rank exist below Helper, since training mode is already built?
questions.suggested: Yes, rank 'Trainee' between Ember and Helper.
questions.why: A safe place for new staff.

questions.question: Who may hand out staff ranks: the owner only?
questions.suggested: Owner only, in LuckPerms. Admins can never change permissions.
questions.why: A hacked admin account must not be able to make itself owner.

questions.question: What happens to rank perks if a payment is charged back?
questions.suggested: Remove the rank and perks, freeze the gems, staff review the account.
questions.why: Needed before the store opens.

questions.question: Should players be able to gift a rank to another player through the store (by Minecraft name)?
questions.suggested: Yes, rank gifts through the store. Gems cannot be given in game.
questions.why: Popular with communities; needs a check so gifts cannot be used to launder chargebacks.

features.feature: Server list MOTD and join flow
features.summary: The server list shows an animated SKYBORNMC / PHOENIX SKYBLOCK message in two lines, with hover text about the status and versions. The server is whitelisted for testing. When a player joins they land at spawn, new players get a welcome title, a broadcast with their join number and welcome lines.

commands.what: MOTD is edited in motd.yml or with /admin. The whitelist is managed with the normal whitelist command.

test: Add the server in Minecraft Java and Bedrock. Check the two MOTD lines, animated gradient and hover text.
Check the player count and version text. Check the icon.
Join with a new account (whitelisted): welcome title, broadcast 'Welcome <name> to Phoenix Skyblock (#N)', welcome lines with clickable /menu and /help.
Leave and join again: 'Welcome back' title.
Try a non-whitelisted account: you should see a clear message that the server is in testing.
Join with an old Java version (1.20) and a new one (1.21.5+): old gets a friendly kick message, new joins.
Check join/quit lines: only ranked players have them.

questions.question: When should the whitelist go off, and should there be a 'beta' mode for friends before launch?
questions.suggested: Keep the whitelist until the closed beta; then open it with a launch countdown in the MOTD.
questions.why: Controls who sees the unfinished server.

questions.question: Which text should the final launch MOTD show (name, 'Season 1', date, versions)?
questions.suggested: 'PHOENIX SKYBLOCK - Season 1 starts DATE - Java and Bedrock'. Countdown is built in.
questions.why: The MOTD is the first ad people see.

questions.question: Is the claim 'Java 1.21.5 - 26.3 + Bedrock' what you want to show, or only 'Java and Bedrock'?
questions.suggested: 'Java & Bedrock', with version details on the website.
questions.why: Versions change; wrong claims create support questions.

questions.question: Should there be a maintenance mode with its own MOTD and kick message, joinable only by staff?
questions.suggested: Yes, a one-command maintenance mode.
questions.why: Needed for updates and restarts.

questions.question: Should the MOTD show the real max player count (350 now), or a lower number to look busy?
questions.suggested: Show the real number. Be honest.
questions.why: Trust and transparency.

questions.question: Should vanished staff and AFK players count in the MOTD player count?
questions.suggested: Do not count vanished staff.
questions.why: Avoids revealing hidden staff.

questions.question: Should all players be teleported to spawn on join (as built), or return to where they logged out?
questions.suggested: Spawn on join (already decided).
questions.why: Confirms the join flow and keeps spawn busy with the shops.

questions.question: Should the first-join welcome lines include a short rules reminder and a link to the website?
questions.suggested: Yes, one line: 'Be kind. /rules'.
questions.why: Players agree to the rules from the first minute.

questions.question: Should the join title and sound be off for returning players who joined many times (to reduce noise)?
questions.suggested: Yes: only the 'Welcome back' title the first time each day.
questions.why: Daily repetition is annoying.

questions.question: Should the server show a short 'Season 1 pre-season ends in X days' line on join during the pre-season week?
questions.suggested: Yes.
questions.why: The pre-season has a wipe at the end; players should be told.

features.summary: Each player sees a sidebar that changes with where they are: spawn, their own island, someone else's island, The Depths (gate, mine, forest, combat) and the warzone. It shows name and rank, money, crystals, gems, island level and, on the island, the next to-do note. Players can turn the scoreboard off in /settings.

commands.what: Turn the scoreboard on/off with /settings scoreboard. Layouts are edited in messages/hud.yml.

test: Join and look at the scoreboard at spawn: Profile (name, rank, money, crystals, gems) and Island (level).
Go to your island: layout changes, and a 'Next:' note line appears when you have an open island note and the setting is on.
Visit someone else's island: 'Visiting: <island>' is shown.
Go to The Depths gate, mine, forest and combat zones: each has its own layout.
Teleport quickly between places: no flicker.
Switch profile: money, crystals and name change at once.
Turn the scoreboard off in /settings and on again.
Bedrock: check all lines fit, symbols are visible and nothing is cut at the edge.

questions.question: Should the island board keep showing Gems and Crystals, or only Money plus the island level?
questions.suggested: Money, Crystals and Gems as built (owner UI decision).
questions.why: Space is limited to about 10 lines.

questions.question: Should big numbers be written in full ($1,234,567) or short ($1.2M)?
questions.suggested: Full below $100k, short above (as built).
questions.why: Short numbers fit better, full numbers feel exact.

questions.question: Should the scoreboard show playtime, online count, or the season countdown on any board?
questions.suggested: Season countdown at spawn only.
questions.why: Keeps the board clean.

questions.question: What should the warzone board show when it exists (kills, bounty, event timer, combat level)?
questions.suggested: Kills, bounty, event timer, combat tag status.
questions.why: The board is a placeholder now.

questions.question: Should the Depths board show the satchel fullness with a warning color when it is 90% full?
questions.suggested: Yes: red at 90%.
questions.why: Players lose drops if the satchel is full; a warning helps.

questions.question: Should there be a leaderboard line (island rank) when the island top exists?
questions.suggested: Yes on the island board: 'Rank #34'.
questions.why: Competition is the point of the game.

questions.question: Should staff in staff mode see a different board (reports, TPS, frozen players)?
questions.suggested: Yes, a staff board.
questions.why: Staff need numbers while moderating.

questions.question: Should players be able to pick between two layouts (short and long)?
questions.suggested: No. One layout per place.
questions.why: More choices = more testing.

questions.question: Should the board hide itself when a menu or book is open (Bedrock has little room)?
questions.suggested: No.
questions.why: Not needed unless players complain.

features.summary: The server has five empty (void) worlds: spawn, islands, outposts, The Depths and the warzone. Spawn is a floating medieval castle with protection (no building, no damage, no hunger). Admins can paste the builders' finished builds into the right worlds and wire their spawn points and zones. Builders use build mode to work at spawn.

commands.what: Go to spawn.
Turn build mode on or off in protected worlds such as spawn.
Set the spawn point where you stand.
List worlds, players and load.
Teleport to a world's spawn.
Show every finished build and its state.
Paste a build with FastAsyncWorldEdit (preview + confirm) and wire its metadata. Back up the world first.

test: Type /spawn. Look around the castle. Try to break and place a block: refused. Check you take no damage and do not get hungry.
Jump off the edge: you are teleported back to spawn (below Y 0). Check there is no fall damage at spawn.
Open doors, buttons, levers, signs, an ender chest and a crafting table at spawn: they work. Other chests do not.
As builder: /build, then place and break blocks. /build again to turn it off.
As admin: /skyblock worlds and /skyblock tp islands, depths, warzone. Check each world looks right (time of day, border).
As admin: /skyblock builds list and /skyblock builds info spawn_base_v1. Only paste on the test server after a backup.
Check the border: walk or fly toward the edge of spawn (1,000 blocks wide) and The Depths (2,000).
Bedrock: walk through the castle and check doors/buttons work with taps.

questions.question: mob_griefing is off in every world. That also stops villagers from farming, sheep from eating grass, foxes from picking berries and zombies from breaking doors. Keep it off everywhere?
questions.suggested: Keep it off on spawn, Depths and warzone. On islands turn it on so villager farms work, and control TNT/creepers with the island 'explosions' setting.
questions.why: Villager and animal farms are a big part of skyblock; this gamerule breaks them.

questions.question: Should /shop, /sell, /bank and /ah work from anywhere by command, or only when you stand at the NPC in the spawn market?
questions.suggested: Commands work anywhere. NPCs are a nice way in that opens the same menus.
questions.why: Defines how much players must travel back to spawn.

questions.question: Time of day is fixed: spawn always noon, The Depths always night, warzone always dusk. OK?
questions.suggested: Yes.
questions.why: Sets the look and mood of each world.

questions.question: Skip the death screen (instant respawn, as now) and do you want death messages in chat anywhere (for example in the warzone only)?
questions.suggested: Instant respawn. Death messages only in the warzone.
questions.why: Vanilla death messages are off. The warzone feels dead without kill messages.

questions.question: Backups today are once a day (04:30), kept 7 days, on the same machine. Is that enough for launch?
questions.suggested: Every 6 hours, kept 7 days, plus an off-site copy and a backup before every update.
questions.why: A single dead disk could lose all player islands and money.

questions.question: What should the unfinished castle districts be used for: Tavern, Hall of Heroes, Keep, Statue, Crate Yard?
questions.suggested: Tavern: quest board and AFK pool; Hall of Heroes: top-3 statues and leaderboards; Keep: rules, news and staff office; Statue: the Phoenix with the server story; Crate Yard: all crates.
questions.why: Builders need to know what to build next.

questions.question: Should wandering traders spawn on islands (they do now)?
questions.suggested: Off. They bring random items that skip parts of the economy.
questions.why: Decide before players find the trader trick.

questions.question: Should Elytra, wind charges and ender pearls work at spawn (it floats in the void)?
questions.suggested: Block elytra and wind charges at spawn; allow pearls only to stay on the castle.
questions.why: Players flying off or using items to cross protected areas.

questions.question: Ender chests and crafting tables at spawn work for everyone today. Is that OK even though /ec and /craft are donor perks?
questions.suggested: Yes at spawn only: a few ender chests and tables at the market are fine.
questions.why: Makes new players feel the perk value without giving it away everywhere.

questions.question: Should players be able to fly at spawn (rank perk) or never?
questions.suggested: Never at spawn for players; staff only.
questions.why: Spawn is full of NPCs and holograms; flyers will clip through it.

questions.question: Should players see a short title when entering a district (Market Square, Forge Quarter)?
questions.suggested: Yes, a short subtitle.
questions.why: Helps orientation; builders already marked the plots.

questions.question: Should the warzone be reachable only by portal/NPC from spawn, not by /spawn or /tpa?
questions.suggested: Yes, only through the portal at the castle.
questions.why: Keeps PvP opt-in and under the safe-zone rules.

questions.question: Which worlds are wiped at the season reset: islands and outposts only, or also The Depths drops and the warzone state?
questions.suggested: Islands and outposts wiped. Depths, spawn and warzone kept; their player data resets.
questions.why: Decides what the season reset script does.

features.feature: Staff mode, freeze, inspect and player reports
features.summary: Staff mode swaps a staff member's inventory for moderation tools (inspect, freeze, random player, logs, vanish, punish, reports). Freeze holds a player for a check: they cannot move, build, use commands or take damage, and their chat goes only to staff. Players can report others with /report, and staff claim, handle and close reports.

commands.what: Turn staff mode on or off.
Freeze or unfreeze a player.
Open a player card: rank, playtime, platform, ping, location, inventory, ender chest, punish, logs.
Report a player with a reason picker or typed text.
Report list, claim and close with an outcome.

test: As helper: /staffmode. Your inventory is swapped for the staff hotbar and you are vanished with night vision. Leave and check your items return exactly.
In staff mode right-click a player with the blaze rod (Inspect) and with the breeze rod (Punish). On Bedrock tap the player.
Freeze a test account: it cannot move, build, use commands, take damage or chat publicly; staff see its chat. Relog while frozen: still frozen. Unfreeze: 10 seconds without fall damage.
Ban the frozen account: the freeze is cleared.
As a normal player: /report <name> hacking. Pick a reason. Report again within 60 seconds: refused. Make 4 open reports: the 4th is refused.
As staff: /reports, claim, close with 'punished' or 'invalid'. The reporter is told the result (also later on join).
Close 3 reports from the same player as 'invalid': staff get a suggestion for the report-abuse reason.
Crash your client while in staff mode (kill the game) and join again: your inventory is restored.

questions.question: Should a freeze end by itself after a time (for example 15 minutes) or alert staff that someone has been frozen for a long time?
questions.suggested: Alert staff at 10 minutes; never auto-unfreeze, never auto-ban.
questions.why: A forgotten freeze keeps a player stuck forever.

questions.question: Should a player need a minimum playtime (for example 10 minutes) before they can use /report?
questions.suggested: 10 minutes.
questions.why: Report spam from brand new or troll accounts.

questions.question: Should reports about staff members go only to admins instead of the normal report list?
questions.suggested: Yes: reports about helper/mod/admin go to admins only.
questions.why: Staff should not handle reports about their colleagues.

questions.question: Which report reasons should be in the picker (today: Hacking, X-ray, Toxicity, Spam, Advertising, Exploiting, Inappropriate build/name, Other)?
questions.suggested: Add: Griefing, Scamming, AFK macro/farm, Bug abuse, Real-world threats.
questions.why: They match the punishment reasons so staff can click straight through.

questions.question: What should a frozen player be told to do, since Discord screen-sharing comes later?
questions.suggested: Until Discord opens: message 'A staff member will talk to you in chat/voice. Stay here.'
questions.why: The freeze message must say something useful.

questions.question: Can any staff member unfreeze a player, or only the one who froze them?
questions.suggested: Any helper or above can unfreeze, logged with the name.
questions.why: A staff member who goes offline should not leave a player frozen.

questions.question: Should staff in staff mode be blocked from using /ah, /pay, /shop, /sell (to keep moderation separate from playing)?
questions.suggested: Yes while in staff mode.
questions.why: Stops staff from using the economy while using powers.

questions.question: How long should a closed report remain visible in /reports (100 shown now) and be kept in the database?
questions.suggested: Keep closed reports 1 year, show the last 100.
questions.why: Reports are evidence for appeals.

questions.question: Should the reporter be told the exact outcome (punished / warned / no evidence) or only 'handled'?
questions.suggested: Say 'handled' for punished and warned, and 'no evidence found' otherwise, never the punishment.
questions.why: Protects the privacy of the reported player.

questions.question: Should staff be able to use Inspect on other staff?
questions.suggested: Yes, but it is logged and admins are told.
questions.why: Prevents silent snooping between staff.

questions.question: Should the number of open reports show on the staff scoreboard and tab?
questions.suggested: Yes: 'Reports: 4' on a staff board.
questions.why: Staff see work waiting without typing a command.

features.summary: Staff open one menu with /p <player> and click a reason. Each reason has a ladder (for example warn, mute 1h, mute 1d). The system picks the next step from the player's history, keeps a warning counter, shows a 2-minute [Undo], protects against double punishing, saves chat evidence, and asks an admin to approve big punishments. Players get a clear ban or mute screen with an ID and a link to appeal.

commands.what: Open the single-screen punishment menu.
Apply a reason directly (-s silent, -ip IP ban, -force skip the double-click protection).
Direct commands (helpers: warn, kick, mute; mods: ban; admins: IP ban).
Lift a punishment (reason required).
Warn counter and waiting suggestions with [Apply] / [Dismiss].
All punishments with who, why and evidence.
Accounts sharing an IP.
Staff punishment numbers.
See your own mute and warnings; confirm a warning.

test: As helper: /p <test account> and look at the layout: mutes top-left, warn buttons bottom-left, bans top-right, small stuff bottom-right, head and warn counter in the middle.
Click Toxicity: the player gets a warning, a title and chat line. Click [Undo] within 2 minutes. After 2 minutes the Undo is gone.
Warn the same player twice: staff get a suggestion 'mute 1h' with [Apply] / [Dismiss]. Apply it.
Have two staff punish the same player within 15 seconds: the second is blocked unless they click again.
As mod: /p <player> hacking. A 30-day ban is a request for an admin ([Approve]/[Deny]); a 7-day ban is applied.
As the punished test account: read the ban screen (ID, appeal link), then /mypunishments and /ack.
As staff: /history <player> and click an entry to see the evidence lines. IPs must not show.
Try to punish an admin: refused (exempt).
Bedrock: open /p with a tap and check slots, icons and Undo on the head.

questions.question: Should the public ban/mute announcement show the reason (for example 'Steve was banned for Hacking') or only that the player was banned?
questions.suggested: Show the rule category only (for example 'Rule 2') without staff name.
questions.why: Shaming vs transparency; the rule number gives players a clear lesson.

questions.question: Should there be a top 'severe' reason (real-life threats, child safety, doxxing) that bans permanently at once and always needs an admin's approval?
questions.suggested: Yes: one reason with an instant permanent ban, approval by an admin, and the evidence kept.
questions.why: Some cases must not climb a ladder.

questions.question: Should bans of 7 days or longer require evidence (a log id, screenshot link or a note) before they can be applied?
questions.suggested: Yes for 7 days or more; mutes and shorter bans do not need it.
questions.why: Protects players and staff when an appeal comes.

questions.question: Can helpers temp-ban for up to 1 day when no mod is online (today helpers cannot ban at all)?
questions.suggested: No. Helpers freeze, mute and kick and call a mod.
questions.why: Keeps ban power with fewer people.

questions.question: Should hacking and x-ray bans be permanent on the first offence when staff are sure (instead of 30 days first)?
questions.suggested: Keep the ladder, but let admins skip steps with a typed reason.
questions.why: Cheaters waiting out a 30-day ban come back.

questions.question: Should shadow mutes (the player thinks chat works but nobody sees it) exist?
questions.suggested: No. Always an honest mute with a message.
questions.why: Transparent punishments are easier to defend.

questions.question: Should a ban also hide the player's island from the visit browser while the ban lasts?
questions.suggested: Yes, hidden while banned, restored after unban.
questions.why: Banned players' islands should not stay on the showcase list.

questions.question: What should happen to a banned player's island: stay as it is, or be locked and frozen for visitors?
questions.suggested: Locked for visitors. Team members keep playing.
questions.why: Teams must not lose their island because of one member.

questions.question: Should the player be able to see which rule number a warning belongs to (yes today) and a short explanation on /rules?
questions.suggested: Yes: each rule has a 2 line explanation on the website.
questions.why: Players accept punishments better when the rule is clear.

questions.question: Should the punishment history count toward being allowed to join team islands or use /ah (for example banned for scamming = no /ah for 30 days)?
questions.suggested: Yes: scamming and RMT reasons also apply a 30 day trade block (sanctions exist).
questions.why: Connects chat/gameplay punishments to the economy.

features.feature: Punishment safeguards: appeals, lockdown, watchlist, guard and reports
features.summary: Players can appeal bans and mutes in game. Staff can start a chat or join lockdown during a raid (only new accounts are affected), keep a private watchlist, add private notes, punish many players at once, and check each other: a guard limits how many punishments one staff member can give in 5 minutes, and admins can roll back a staff member's recent punishments. A monthly report shows the numbers.

commands.what: Appeal your mute or ban (20 to 500 characters).
Staff queue: read, Accept / Reduce / Deny.
Raid lockdown for new accounts only.
Private watchlist; staff get a line when the player joins.
Private staff notes.
Punish up to 20 players at once with a confirm.
Suggest a punishment (console, anticheat, staff); never applied automatically.
Choose which staff alerts you receive.
Lift a block, lock or unlock a staff member's punishments.
Undo a staff member's recent punishments (preview first).
Owner: delete a player's personal data on request.
Monthly punishment report; give back a sanction.

test: As a muted test account: /appeal and read what can be appealed. Send an appeal text under 20 characters (refused), then a proper one. Staff see it in /appeals and Accept, Reduce or Deny with a reason.
Start /lockdown chat 5m. A brand-new account cannot chat or /msg; an older or ranked account can. /lockdown off ends it.
Start /lockdown join 2m: an account that never joined cannot join (friendly 'server is busy' screen), returning players can.
/watch <player> reason, then have that player join: staff see one line. The player is never told. /watchlist shows the list.
/pnote <player> text; /pnote <player> shows notes with [Remove].
/pbulk spam <player1> <player2>: a confirm screen with each player's step, then [Undo all].
As helper punish 6 players in 5 minutes: the guard blocks you after the limit. An admin runs /pguard allow <name>.
As admin: /prollback <staff> 1h shows a preview; confirm to undo.
Check /preport lists last month with no player names.

questions.question: On launch day many new accounts join at once. Should raid detection (alert at 15 new accounts in 30 seconds) be raised or off for the first week?
questions.suggested: Raise to 60 new accounts in 30 seconds during launch week, then back to 15.
questions.why: Otherwise staff get false raid alerts and may lock out real players.

questions.question: Should permanent bans be appealable, and after how long?
questions.suggested: Yes after 30 days, decided by an admin. Cheating bans after 90 days.
questions.why: A fair second chance, but not too soon.

questions.question: Should appeals be decided by mods (as now) or by a small appeal team of admins and senior mods?
questions.suggested: Mods for mutes and bans up to 30 days; admins for longer bans.
questions.why: Appeals often come from angry players; a second pair of eyes helps.

questions.question: Are the guard limits right: helper 5 bans / 15 mutes in 5 minutes, mod 10 / 25, admin alert only?
questions.suggested: Yes, with /pguard allow before planned cleanups.
questions.why: Too low blocks honest staff on a bad night; too high does not protect.

questions.question: Should a staff member who is blocked by the guard be automatically told to contact an admin through a button?
questions.suggested: Yes: [Contact admin] sends an alert.
questions.why: A blocked helper should not have to find an admin by chat.

questions.question: Should the 'Honorable' title (60 days without a punishment, 10 hours played) give a small reward as well?
questions.suggested: Yes: 500 crystals and a cosmetic particle.
questions.why: Rewards good behaviour, not only punishes bad.

questions.question: Should the lockdown also stop new accounts from creating islands or using /pay and /ah?
questions.suggested: Yes during a chat lockdown: no /pay, /ah, /trade for new accounts.
questions.why: Raiders often try to scam or duplicate quickly.

questions.question: Should watchlist entries expire after 30 days (as now) or stay until removed?
questions.suggested: Expire after 30 days; one click to renew.
questions.why: Stale entries cause bias.

features.summary: Everything players and staff do is written to a log: chat, commands, money, trades, auctions, island actions, item life, punishments, staff actions and logins. Staff search it with /logs by player, time, category, near me, island or item, and can click a chat line to punish. Admins can export to CSV.

commands.what: Open the log viewer: pick who, category and time range.
Everything a player did.
Money between players.
Trades, chat or commands of a player.
Island actions, life of a unique item, actions near you.
Everything a staff member did.
CSV file to the exports folder (logged).
Next pages in chat (console, Bedrock).

test: Do a few things: chat, /pay a friend, use a command. As helper /logs player <you> chat 1h: your lines show. Money lines need mod.
Click a chat line of a test account: the punish menu opens with that line as evidence.
/logs near 30 1h while standing where a friend placed and broke blocks. Check results and click to teleport (mods).
Look up a unique item: /logs item <uuid> shows its whole life (made, traded, sold).
As admin: /logs export <name> and check the CSV in plugins/PhoenixSkyblock/exports.
Check that a helper cannot see IPs or economy lines, and a mod cannot see staff logs.
Bedrock: open the viewer by tap, or use the chat output (/logs page).

questions.question: IP addresses and login history are kept forever (decided for security). Norwegian/EU law normally wants a limit and a privacy policy. Which limit do you want?
questions.suggested: Keep IPs 12 months after the player's last login (and for the length of any ban plus 12 months), then delete. Publish a privacy policy on the website. I am not a lawyer; please check.
questions.why: Keeping personal data forever without a reason can be illegal under GDPR.

questions.question: Should every lookup (/logs, /inspect, /whois, /invsee) be recorded so admins can see which staff looked at which player?
questions.suggested: Yes, admins can see 'who looked at whom' for 12 months.
questions.why: Protects players from staff snooping.

questions.question: Chat, command and item logs are searchable for 30 days and then archived to files. How long should the archive be kept?
questions.suggested: Keep archives 12 months, then delete.
questions.why: Disk space and privacy limits.

questions.question: Should the life of valuable unique items (tools, enchant books, notes, set tokens) be searchable longer than 30 days?
questions.suggested: Yes: 180 days for unique items, since dupes are found late.
questions.why: Dupe investigations often start weeks after the dupe.

questions.question: Should players get a notice on first join that chat, commands and actions are logged, with a link to the privacy policy?
questions.suggested: Yes, one line and a link.
questions.why: People should know before they type.

questions.question: Should a player be able to ask for a copy of the data you hold about them (a 'data request') and how is that handled?
questions.suggested: Yes: they open a ticket, an admin exports with /logs export and /history and sends it.
questions.why: GDPR gives players this right.

questions.question: Should private messages be searchable by mods in /logs without a report (today: socialspy live and 30 days logged)?
questions.suggested: Only with a reason typed in the search that is also logged.
questions.why: Private messages deserve extra protection.

questions.question: Should the CSV export be blocked for players' private messages?
questions.suggested: Yes, exports never include private messages.
questions.why: Exports leave the server, which raises the privacy risk.

questions.question: Should the log viewer show a 'staff note' button so staff can attach a comment to a log line for a case?
questions.suggested: Yes later: pin a line to a case with a comment.
questions.why: Cases that take days need the evidence in one place.
